shared_statistical_model.source_location: ESA printed page 12:2, Robust Multivariate Polynomial Regression Problem
shared_statistical_model.domain_and_degree: n and d are positive integers; p is a real polynomial on [-1,1]^n with each coordinate degree at most d (individual degree, not total degree).
shared_statistical_model.locations: M sample locations are independent with a common specified probability law chi on the cube.
shared_statistical_model.support: Each sample is marked an outlier independently with probability rho. The clean-design location law is not replaced by an adversary.
shared_statistical_model.labels: After all locations are available, an adversary may choose every label; inlier labels must satisfy |y_i-p(x_i)| <= sigma and outlier labels are unrestricted.
shared_statistical_model.output_and_goal: Return a polynomial in the same individual-degree class with cube sup-norm error at most C*sigma, uniformly over the unknown polynomial and admissible labels, with the stated success probability.
shared_statistical_model.noise_scope: The original problem definition has sigma > 0. The upper-bound theorems explicitly extend to sigma >= 0. The sample lower-bound candidates below use sigma > 0; they do not assert a sigma=0 lower bound.
shared_statistical_model.dimension_scope: The paper emphasizes constant n > 1, and the S7 rate comparison fixes n. The displayed lower-bound constants are c(C) and c(C,rho), respectively; no extra n-dependence is inserted into those displayed constants.

quantifiers_and_hypotheses: For every fixed approximation factor C > 1 there exists c=c(C)>0.
Use the shared statistical model with uniform cube locations, sigma>0, and any rho in [0,1].
The learner must solve the problem for all individual-degree-d targets and all admissible labels with success probability strictly greater than 2/3.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.statement_paraphrase: Every such algorithm needs M >= (c*d)^(2*n) samples. The assertion includes rho=0, which means absence of outliers, not absence of bounded inlier noise.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.fixed_parameter_use: Set C=2+epsilon. For fixed n and epsilon, c^(2*n)>0 is independent of d, so this is a d^(2*n) lower bound. P34's uniform upper bound has that polynomial exponent, with an extra occupancy logarithm.
not_claimed: No joint optimality in n, epsilon, rho, or delta
No lower bound for noiseless sigma=0 recovery
quantitative_comparison_candidates.formal_dependency_reason: The published universal statistical-algorithm lower-bound model is not a Lean dependency in this repository. A replacement broad algorithm predicate would not certify the actual theorem. It is a secondary comparison, so no new axiom or mock model is introduced.

quantifiers_and_hypotheses: For every C>1 and every rho>0 within the probability range of the shared model, there exists c=c(C,rho)>0.
For each probability law chi on [-1,1]^n, a learner receives iid locations with that law; sigma>0 and the shared adversarial-label model apply.
The learner must solve the problem uniformly over targets and admissible labels with success probability strictly greater than 2/3.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.statement_paraphrase: The necessary sample count is M >= (c*d)^n * log d, for any location law. For the nontrivial S7 application restrict to 0<rho<1/2.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.fixed_parameter_use: For fixed n, epsilon and positive rho, set C=2+epsilon. The positive factor c^n is independent of d. With constant failure probability this matches the product-Chebyshev upper rate's d^n*log d dependence.
not_claimed: The logarithmic lower bound at rho=0
A constant uniform as rho approaches 0 or 1/2
An adaptive-query or adversarial-design lower bound outside the published iid-location problem
quantitative_comparison_candidates.formal_dependency_reason: Same published statistical lower-bound model issue as ESA2024_1_6_uniform_sample_lower; the comparison is documented rather than replaced by a formally weaker artificial algorithm class.

quantitative_comparison_candidates.locator: Theorem 1.11, printed 12:5; arXiv v1 Theorem 1.8 and proof on PDF pages 16-17
quantifiers_and_hypotheses: There is an absolute constant A such that for every positive n,d, every integer m>=d, and every real individual-degree-at-most-d polynomial q the following holds.
Use the Cartesian product of Chebyshev-extrema intervals with endpoints cos(pi*j/m). In each cell C_j choose an arbitrary point a_j.

r is the corresponding well-defined cellwise constant function q(a_j). The printed source assumes r exists and has the specified constant restriction on each cell; a partition boundary convention must be consistent.

critical_formula_check.evidence: The official PDF rendered on printed page 12:5 has d and n at the same baseline. The arXiv v1 proof also telescopes across n coordinate changes, bounding each change by A*d/m times the global sup norm.
critical_formula_check.warning: PDF search/extraction may join the letters as dn or misleadingly display d^n. The rendered formula and coordinate-sum proof determine the reading.

quantitative_comparison_candidates.own_use: Unnormalized Lebesgue cube volume is 2^n, so its L1 error is bounded by 2^n times this uniform error. This is the first inequality of S7.E1 after n-only constants are suppressed.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.formal_dependency_reason: The external source theorem is not imported. P34 already has internally proved actual cell-oscillation estimates from the precisely documented standard trigonometric Bernstein input. The short comparison module only composes numerical inequalities; it does not assume or replace the new multivariate Chebyshev L1 norming theorem.

quantitative_comparison_candidates.locator: Theorem 1.12, printed 12:5; norm convention in Definition 2.1, printed 12:11; arXiv v1 Theorem 1.9
quantifiers_and_hypotheses: There exists a global B>0, independent of n,d,q.
For every positive integer n, positive integer d and real polynomial q with degree at most d in every coordinate on [-1,1]^n.
The L1 norm is the integral of |q| against unnormalized n-dimensional Lebesgue measure, as defined in the source; it is not the product-Chebyshev norm.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.degree_zero_note: Positive d is retained. The bare formula with d=0 would be false for nonzero constants; constant polynomials can instead be viewed in the d=1 class.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.own_use: Combine with ESA2024_1_11_cellwise_sup_proxy and the cube volume. An n-only coefficient K_n=2^n*A*B^n*n multiplies d^(2*n+1)/m times the Lebesgue L1 norm.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.formal_dependency_reason: The published Lebesgue Nikolskii inequality is used only to explain the previous algorithm's degree loss. The new main proof uses an internally proved actual Fourier/Chebyshev conversion. No corresponding external Lean axiom is needed or added for this discussion.

quantifiers_and_hypotheses: epsilon in (0,1/2], delta in (0,epsilon], sigma>=0, eta>0, and 0<=rho<1/2; n,d positive integers and the shared degree and label model.
The location law is either product-Chebyshev or the uniform cube law.
The constants in the displayed O notation may depend on n and rho.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.statement_paraphrase: Algorithm 2 returns a polynomial in the same degree class with sup error <=(2+epsilon)*sigma+eta with probability >=1-delta. Sufficient samples are O_(n,rho)((d/epsilon)^n*log(d/delta)) for product-Chebyshev and O_(n,rho)((d/epsilon)^(2*n)*log(d/delta)) for uniform locations.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.runtime_as_printed: Theorem 3.1 states O(log_(1/epsilon)(||p||_infinity/eta)) LPs, each with (d+1)^n<M variables and M constraints.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.runtime_endpoint_caveat: The printed logarithm requires the usual saturation at a constant number of calls for small or zero signal. Do not treat the unsaturated display as a nonnegative count for every p. Choosing eta proportional to sigma to eliminate the additive tolerance additionally requires suitable noise-scale information.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.formal_dependency_reason: The existing algorithm and its correctness are comparison objects, not dependencies of P34's new algorithm. This register records the published statement and its runtime endpoint convention without creating a mock estimator proof.

quantifiers_and_hypotheses: epsilon in (0,1/2], delta in (0,epsilon], sigma>=0, and 0<=rho<1/2; positive n,d and the shared model.
Use the product-Chebyshev or uniform location law; constants may depend on n and rho.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.statement_paraphrase: Algorithm 4 gives sup error <=(2+epsilon)*sigma with probability >=1-delta. Samples suffice at O_(n,rho)((d^(2*n+1)/epsilon)^n*log(d/delta)) for product-Chebyshev and O_(n,rho)((d^(2*n+1)/epsilon)^(2*n)*log(d/delta)) for uniform locations. Runtime is polynomial in M and log_epsilon(1-2*rho), without a signal-scale or eta parameter.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.formal_dependency_reason: This is the published larger-sample baseline, not an input to the new recovery proof. A local registry can document it exactly without encoding all of the previous algorithm as an assumed universal estimator.

quantitative_comparison_candidates.locator: Theorem 5.2 and following discussion, printed 12:15-12:16; arXiv v1 Theorem 6.4
quantifiers_and_hypotheses: Use 0<epsilon<1/2, 0<alpha<1/2 and sigma>=0. The printed theorem abbreviates the ranges as epsilon,alpha<1/2; positivity is retained from the meaningful accuracy/good-sample setup.
The finite data set S has bounded inlier noise sigma for some p in the individual-degree-d class, and is alpha-good for the (m,n)-Chebyshev partition.
Source Definition 2.7 requires at least 1/alpha samples per cell and strictly fewer than an alpha fraction of outliers in each cell.
For a sufficiently large absolute c>1, m >= (c*d)^(2*n+1)/epsilon.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.statement_paraphrase: Algorithm 4 returns a degree-d polynomial with sup error <=(2+epsilon)*sigma after O(n*log_(1/epsilon)d + log_epsilon(1-2*alpha)) iterations.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.necessity_caveat: This is a sufficient hypothesis for that published initializer and proof. S7's word 'requires' is method-specific: neither this theorem nor the upper inequalities in (7.1) prove that every Lebesgue L1 discretization or every algorithm needs this grid size.
quantitative_comparison_candidates.formal_dependency_reason: The existing algorithm's sufficient grid condition is documented as an external comparison. The new grid scale is proved within P34 and is not supplied by this candidate.

discussion_and_background.paraphrase: The remark asks for a multivariate analogue of combining optimal sample complexity with runtime independent of signal-to-noise ratio, as achieved by KKP in one variable. It points out the sample blowup of the scale-independent algorithm.
discussion_and_background.scope: An open-question statement, not a theorem input. P34 answers it in its expressly stated exact-real LP-oracle model; this does not import a finite-precision guarantee.

discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Historical noisy algebraic curve fitting and list/multiple-curve recovery, including mixture-model questions. S7 invokes no numerical theorem from this paper.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Historical attribution only; no lemma is applied.

discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Earlier algorithms for noisy algebraic and trigonometric curve fitting with randomly supported label outliers. S7 asserts no quantitative outlier threshold or error factor from it.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Historical attribution only. Its additional noise/range restrictions are not transferred to or removed from P34 by an assumed theorem.

discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Multidimensional polynomial representation of noisy and Byzantine data, with extensions of error-correcting interpolation and curve-fitting methods.
discussion_and_background.publication_note: Published online November 2016; journal issue is Acta Informatica 55 (2018), pp.213-225, consistent with the source bibliography.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: S7 uses this as history, without importing a recovery theorem.

locators: Lemma 2.1, PDF pp.5-6 and Appendix A
discussion_and_background.paraphrase: The one-variable antecedent uses arbitrary Chebyshev-interval representatives, interval-Lebesgue-length-weighted absolute residual minimization, and iterative median correction.
discussion_and_background.precision_note: Its Lemma 2.1 concerns a single univariate degree-d polynomial, m>=d, arbitrary representatives in each Chebyshev interval, and a relative Lebesgue Lq proxy estimate for q>=1. It is not a joint multivariate representative theorem. Its LAD weights are interval lengths, rather than the new product-Chebyshev cell masses.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: S7 credits the construction. P34 proves its own actual multivariate norming and estimator arguments instead of importing this univariate theorem as the new result.

discussion_and_background.locator: Definition 1 and informal Theorem 3, PDF pp.2-3
discussion_and_background.paraphrase: After iid pairs are drawn, an adversary can replace a fraction of complete pairs. Under certifiable hypercontractivity of the covariates (and the theorem's label/bit-complexity conditions), the objective is population squared prediction risk relative to the best linear fit.
discussion_and_background.scope: Population squared loss is not a cube-wide sup guarantee. Merely ordinary hypercontractivity is not substituted for the certifiable assumption of the algorithmic theorem.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Model/loss comparison only; S7 imports none of the numerical risk bounds or SoS guarantees.

discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Strong contamination replaces selected sample objective functions after observation. The general guarantee is an approximate critical point for a population objective, given an approximate empirical critical-point learner and uniform gradient regularity.
discussion_and_background.scope_conditions: Theorem 2.1 uses a good subset of size >=(1-epsilon)N, gradient covariance <=sigma^2 I and good-mean gradient error <=sigma*sqrt(epsilon), uniformly over a closed parameter domain; objective functions are bounded below. This differs from bounded label noise for a fixed polynomial on a cube.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Qualitative setting comparison only. No population critical-point theorem is used to assert P34's uniform recovery.

discussion_and_background.locator: Problem model and Theorems 1.2-1.3, PDF pp.2-3
discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Gaussian linear regression with adversarial replacement of complete samples, independent Gaussian response noise, and Euclidean coefficient-vector error. Known and unknown covariance have different algorithmic requirements.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Only the distinct data model and loss criterion are compared; no quantitative theorem is imported.

discussion_and_background.locator: Abstract, problem setup, robust gradient descent theorem and regression applications
discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Robust gradient estimation yields population-risk parameter recovery under contamination or heavy-tailed observations; the general convergence argument assumes appropriate risk curvature and gradient-estimation error control.
discussion_and_background.version_note: The author preprint inspected is April 2018 v2; the bibliography names the 2020 JRSS B journal publication. No theorem numbering is transferred between them.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Background comparison of objectives and corruption models; no population-risk estimate is an input to P34.

discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Trigonometric MZ inequalities for nonuniform grids under regularity/perturbation conditions, with interpolation and Besov-space consequences.
discussion_and_background.scope: The cited grid regularity conditions and exponent ranges cannot be dropped to obtain P34's arbitrary joint representatives.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Literature placement only. No background MZ theorem replaces the source's own endpoint L1 tensor argument.

discussion_and_background.locator: Theorem 13, PDF pp.11-12; Theorem 15, PDF p.17
discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Sampling norm inequalities for triangular node families on the unit circle, with separation and lower-density hypotheses; also stability under sufficiently small perturbations.
discussion_and_background.scope: The density/separation framework concerns node families, not prescribed multivariate Chebyshev product cells with arbitrarily coupled representatives.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Related literature only; no density theorem is a Lean premise.

discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Multivariate MZ results construct/select sampling nodes with weights on suitable domains. The source cites this for context, without asserting its results for all jointly selected points in prescribed product cells.
discussion_and_background.version_note: Author-hosted draft is dated August 2017; journal citation is Acta Mathematica Hungarica 154(1), 69-89 (2018). The author's publication-list volume text differs, so the source DOI is retained as the publication identifier.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Existence of selected nodes is not an input that proves the new arbitrary-representative conclusion. No theorem is imported.

discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Sampling discretization of finite-dimensional Lp subspaces under Nikolskii-type assumptions; probabilistic/chaining methods give sampling results.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Listed sampling-discretization background. S7 invokes no particular cardinality theorem, and no existential sampling set is substituted for arbitrary prescribed-cell representatives.

discussion_and_background.locator: Abstract, introductory sampling problem and Theorem 1.1, PDF pp.1-3
discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Sampling discretization for finite-dimensional continuous function spaces, including Lp with 1<=p<2 under Nikolskii norm-control assumptions.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Background only; the existence or random construction of good sampling nodes does not provide the prescribed-cell arbitrary-representative theorem.

discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Empirical Lp-moment approximation and sampling discretization for bounded finite-dimensional spaces under norm/embedding assumptions, including random-sampling and sparse-function results.
discussion_and_background.publication_note: The primary arXiv record is v1 dated 29 May 2026 and has no journal reference at inspection. This is documented as the source's cited preprint, not upgraded to an already-published external theorem.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Bibliographic context only. No theorem is used, so no publication exemption or mathematical input is requested.

discussion_and_background.paraphrase: Noiseless unique reconstruction in finite spans of multivariate Chebyshev polynomials using structured nodes from cosine-transformed rank-1 lattices and FFT-based computations.
discussion_and_background.publication_note: The source cites June 2024 v1. Its arXiv record links related DOI 10.1016/j.acha.2025.101761, but that related publication is not silently substituted for the version cited by P34.
discussion_and_background.scope: Unique reconstruction from a structured sampling set is different from robust recovery under arbitrary label outliers and arbitrary joint cell representatives.
discussion_and_background.formal_dependency_reason: Qualitative comparison only; neither the reconstruction algorithm nor a sampling-cardinality theorem is imported.

scope_findings.finding: ESA Theorem 1.11 gives d*n/m. Combined with cube volume and Theorem 1.12 it supports the displayed d^(2*n+1)/m comparison. There is no unsupported switch from d^n/m to d/m.

An upper bound proves a sufficient grid scale, not universal necessity. Read 'requires' in S7.p3/p6 as describing this published initializer/proof's grid hypothesis. The register and Lean module make this direction explicit.
The uniform lower bound holds with rho=0 but still sigma>0. P34's actual sigma=0 recovery is consistent with it.
The d-exponent comparison fixes n,epsilon,rho and a constant success threshold. It supplies no joint optimality claim.
References [3] and [10] are recorded at their cited arXiv versions and are not treated as published theorem exemptions. Reference [10] has a related journal DOI, explicitly distinguished.

own_formal_comparison.claims: Scalar arithmetic only. No statistical algorithm is defined, no published bound is turned into a Lean axiom, and no P34 principal theorem is assumed.
